problem_summary.summary: Swap the left and right subtrees at every node and return the original root.
problem_summary.input_output: Input: a binary-tree root. Return the root of the in-place inverted tree.

brute_force.explanation: Build a new tree recursively, assigning each source right child to the new left side and each source left child to the new right side.
brute_force.correctness_idea: At every source node the constructed node keeps its value and recursively swaps the complete child subtrees, which is the definition of inversion.
brute_force.time_complexity: O(n) — each node is copied once.
brute_force.space_complexity: O(n) for the output tree, plus O(h) recursion stack.

optimized.explanation: Traverse the existing tree and swap the two child references at each node.
optimized.correctness_idea: Each node's children are exchanged exactly once, so every original left path becomes the corresponding right path and vice versa, without changing node values.
optimized.time_complexity: O(n) — every node is visited once.
optimized.space_complexity: O(h) auxiliary recursion stack, with no new tree nodes.

steps.action: Swap child links; recurse into new left child 9.
Leave its links unchanged; return to node 6.
Swap links, producing left 4 and right 1.
Return the root 6 with all links inverted.

edge_cases.handling: Both child links are already null and the root is returned.
The existing child is moved to the opposite side.
